question: The Indian national satellite system (INSAT) program was established in _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1983**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian National Satellite System (INSAT)** was established in **1983** by the Government of India to cater to various needs like telecommunications, broadcasting, meteorology, and disaster warning.
 
• INSAT is a joint venture between the **Department of Space (DOS)** and **India Meteorological Department (IMD)**, alongside other governmental agencies.
 
• The program marked the beginning of India’s **space-based communication era** with INSAT-1B being the first operational satellite launched in **1983** after the failure of INSAT-1A.
 
• INSAT satellites are equipped with **transponders** for telecommunication and broadcasting and provide crucial meteorological data.
 
• It is one of the largest domestic communication satellite systems in the Asia-Pacific region and has greatly enhanced India’s **telecommunication, television broadcasting, and weather forecasting** capabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **INSAT System Overview:**

 
 
• INSAT satellites serve **telecommunication, television broadcasting, meteorology, and disaster warning** purposes.
 
• The system consists of a series of satellites like INSAT-2, INSAT-3, GSAT series, and more, which have contributed to India’s space capabilities over the decades.
 
• INSAT satellites are positioned in **geostationary orbit**, ensuring continuous coverage over the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **First Operational Satellite - INSAT-1B:**
 
 
• INSAT-1B was launched on **August 30, 1983**, on a **Delta rocket** from Cape Canaveral, USA.
 
• It provided services like **telecommunication, television relay, and meteorological observations**.
 
• It marked the first successful satellite of the INSAT series, paving the way for further satellite launches.
 
 
 
• **Applications of INSAT Satellites:**
 
 
• They serve as a backbone for **telecommunication networks** and television broadcasting across India.
 
• **Meteorological payloads** help in weather forecasting, cyclone warnings, and disaster management.
 
• INSAT satellites also support **search and rescue operations** by relaying distress signals.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of INSAT Program:**
 
 
• After the success of INSAT-1B, subsequent satellites like **INSAT-2 and INSAT-3 series** were launched with enhanced capabilities.
 
• Modern satellites like **GSAT** series have advanced features, including high-throughput communication services.
 
• The program has significantly contributed to India’s technological and economic growth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option Analysis:**

 
 
• **1963:** This was the year India launched its first rocket from the **Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS)**. Not relevant to INSAT.
 
• **1972:** India’s **Department of Space** was established in this year, laying the groundwork for INSAT but not the actual launch.
 
• **1983:** This is the correct answer as INSAT became operational with the launch of INSAT-1B, providing communication and meteorological services.
 
• **1997:** INSAT satellites were operational but this year doesn’t mark the establishment of the program.
 
 
 
• **Significance of INSAT:**
 
 
• INSAT has contributed to **economic growth** by enabling efficient telecommunication and broadcasting.
 
• It plays a key role in **disaster warning systems**, saving thousands of lives during natural calamities.
